title: Restore hearing in OTOF-related deafness with an approved gene therapy

concept.text: Restore auditory signalling in people with biallelic OTOF variants and preserved outer hair-cell function. Otarmeni achieved accelerated approval, with durability and effects on speech development requiring continued verification. Proposed completion test: FDA accelerated approval for genetically confirmed OTOF-associated severe-to-profound hearing loss, based on clinically substantial hearing improvement against untreated natural history, with confirmatory durability and functional follow-up required. Test set by: FDA; its assessment included a 24-patient study, with hearing improvement in 80% of the 20 efficacy-evaluable patients. Reported achieved: FDA granted accelerated approval to lunsotogene parvec-cwha (Otarmeni) on 23 April 2026. Sources given: [FDA Otarmeni approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-ever-gene-therapy-treatment-genetic-hearing-loss-under-national-priority-voucher) ; [FDA Otarmeni product and approval record](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/otarmeni).

page.title: Gene therapy for OTOF-related deafness
page.definition: A gene therapy licensed by a regulator improves hearing sensitivity in OTOF-related deafness, which is caused by disease-associated variants in both copies of the gene encoding otoferlin, a protein needed for sound transmission from the inner ear to the auditory nerve. Treatment requires preserved function of outer hair cells, which amplify sound, and no cochlear implant in the treated ear.

goal.need: OTOF variants account for 2%–8% of inherited, nonsyndromic hearing loss. Two nonworking copies disrupt sound transmission from the inner ear. Before 23 April 2026, no disease-modifying treatment existed for OTOF-related deafness.

statements.body: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders
statements.quote: Replacing the faulty otoferlin gene with a functioning version could be an approach to restoring hearing in those with otoferlin-related hearing loss.
Prior to today’s approval, no disease modifying treatments existed for OTOF-related deafness.
statements.context: The announcement accompanied Otarmeni’s accelerated approval on 23 April 2026.

completion.title: FDA licenses a gene therapy for hearing loss caused by biallelic OTOF variants.
completion.criterion: FDA licenses, by traditional or accelerated approval, a gene therapy indicated for pediatric and adult patients with severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss (any frequency >90 dB HL, decibels above normal hearing level) associated with molecularly confirmed biallelic OTOF variants, preserved outer hair cell function and no prior cochlear implant in the same ear. The label reports a study whose primary endpoint is an average pure-tone audiometry threshold ≤70 dB HL across 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 kHz at week 24 (single-arm; 24 children treated, 20 assessed, for the first licence). Verified benefit at 104 weeks, speech and language outcomes and other genetic forms of deafness are not required.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration: accelerated BLA approval letter of 23 April 2026, STN 125874/0, under 21 CFR 601.41, and Otarmeni prescribing information, sections 1 and 14.
completion.threshold_quote: OTARMENI is indicated for the treatment of pediatric and adult patients with severe-to-profound and profound sensorineural hearing loss (any frequency >90 dB HL) associated with molecularly confirmed biallelic variants in the OTOF gene, preserved outer hair cell function, and no prior cochlear implant in the same ear.
completion.basis: A first: FDA announced Otarmeni (lunsotogene parvec-cwha) on 23 April 2026 as the first gene therapy for genetic hearing loss. An accelerated approval is a licence, so it meets this test. It rests on an intermediate endpoint: 16 of 20 assessed children reached ≤70 dB HL at week 24. Continued approval depends on verification: FDA requires 104-week outcomes in at least 30 treated pediatric patients, and in at least 5 newly treated patients aged 16 years or older, covering hearing, speech and language, and quality of life. OTOF variants account for 2%–8% of inherited nonsyndromic hearing loss.

milestones.title: OTOF gene transfer restores reproducible auditory brainstem responses in a deaf animal model.
milestones.criterion: Preclinical proof of concept demonstrates a biological response resembling the intended human response. For OTOF replacement, the readout is a reproducible auditory brainstem response (ABR), an electrical response to sound. Al-Moyed et al., published on 3 December 2018, reported click thresholds of 40–60 dB sound-pressure level in Otof-deficient mice; analysed treated groups contained 17 and 8 mice, with 38 deaf controls. About two thirds of injected knockout mice lacked detectable ABRs and transduction and were classified as controls.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Human Gene Therapy for Rare Diseases, January 2020, section IV: a nonbinding qualitative preclinical recommendation. The OTOF-specific readout is documented by Al-Moyed et al.
milestones.threshold_quote: demonstrate a biological response to the investigational GT product that is similar to the expected response in humans.

milestones.title: Children receive OTOF gene therapy and reach the protocol’s 6-week safety endpoint.
milestones.criterion: Children with biallelic OTOF deafness receive gene therapy under an ethics-approved first-in-human protocol and complete its 6-week dose-limiting toxicity assessment. Toxicity is defined by Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events, version 5.0: haematologic grade ≥4, non-haematologic grade ≥3, or aural grade ≥2. In ChiCTR2200063181, six children enrolled between 19 October 2022 and 9 June 2023 received unilateral AAV1-hOTOF; none developed dose-limiting toxicity, and all completed 26 weeks of follow-up.
milestones.set_by: Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University, ethics-approved protocol [2022]2022085-1, registered as ChiCTR2200063181; primary safety endpoint published by Lv et al.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary endpoint was dose-limiting toxicity at 6 weeks after injection.

milestones.title: Children reach CHORD’s ≤70 dB HL hearing threshold 24 weeks after OTOF gene therapy.
milestones.criterion: CHORD’s primary endpoint is the proportion of children reaching average behavioural pure-tone audiometry thresholds ≤70 dB HL at week 24, averaged across 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 kHz; bilateral recipients are evaluated using the better treated ear. The peer-reviewed report published on 12 October 2025 found 9/12 responders (75%). The subsequent FDA label reports 16/20 responders (80%) among 24 treated children; one missing week-24 outcome was imputed as nonresponse.
milestones.set_by: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, CHORD protocol DB-OTO-001, NCT05788536, primary efficacy endpoint; also specified in section 14 of the FDA-approved Otarmeni label.
milestones.threshold_quote: an average threshold on behavioral pure-tone audiometry (PTA) at week 24 of 70 dB HL or less

not_found: No OTOF-specific numerical animal-efficacy cutoff was found in the FDA guidance or approval documents.
The opened CHORD abstract and FDA label do not state a required trial-level responder proportion.
The NEJM and Lancet publisher pages were inaccessible; the NEJM abstract and a Lancet full-text mirror were accessible.

results.finding: OTOF gene transfer restored reproducible click-evoked ABRs at 40–60 dB SPL in deaf Otof-knockout mice; analysed treated groups contained 17 and 8 mice, with 38 deaf controls.
results.detail: Around two thirds of injected knockout mice had neither detectable ABRs nor transduced cells and were classified as non-transduced controls. The analysed treated groups therefore exclude these unsuccessful injections. ABR wave amplitudes remained reduced.
results.quote: Acoustic clicks evoked auditory brainstem responses with thresholds of 40–60 dB.

results.finding: Dual-AAV OTOF gene transfer restored ABR hearing responses in 5/5 deaf Otof−/− mice treated after hearing onset, assessed 4 weeks later.
results.detail: ABR thresholds resembled wild-type thresholds and remained stable for 20 weeks. Thresholds required clearly repeated ABR peaks, confirmed by offline waveform analysis; wave I amplitudes remained reduced.
results.quote:
ABR recordings 4 wk after injection showed hearing recovery in all of the mice receiving injections on P17 (
n
= 5), with ABR thresholds in response to clicks or tone-burst stimuli remarkably similar to those in wild-type mice

results.finding: Six children received unilateral AAV1-hOTOF; 0 developed dose-limiting toxicity through the 6-week safety endpoint.
results.detail: The ethics-approved first-in-human trial used the specified CTCAE v5.0 toxicity thresholds. All six children completed 26 weeks of follow-up.
results.quote:
All 
participants completed follow-up visits up to week 26. No dose-limiting toxicity or serious adverse events occurred.

results.finding: In the six-child AAV1-hOTOF trial, participant 1 reached an average pure-tone audiometry threshold of 30 dB at week 26.
results.detail: This is a different trial from CHORD and reports week-26 rather than week-24 outcomes. Pure-tone audiometry was available for only three children; it does not establish CHORD’s specified responder endpoint.
results.quote:
The average pure-tone 
audiometry threshold was 71 dB at 4 weeks, 68 dB at 
6 weeks, 55 dB at 13 weeks, and 30 dB at 26 weeks.

results.finding: Among 42 AAV1-hOTOF recipients, including children, no dose-limiting toxicities were observed at the 6-week primary endpoint.
results.detail: Reports ChiCTR2200063181 results, but the supplied text does not establish ethics approval, first-in-human status, the specified CTCAE toxicity definitions, or completion of assessment by every child.
results.quote: The primary end point was dose-limiting toxicity within 6 weeks. The secondary end point assessed efficacy and adverse events. No dose-limiting toxicities were observed.

results.finding: AAV1-hOTOF recipients with hearing recovery had mean behavioural thresholds of 37 ± 5 dB HL at 2.5 years (7 treated ears).
results.detail: This is not CHORD. Results describe a hearing-recovery subset's mean across 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 kHz at 2.5 years, rather than the proportion of children reaching ≤70 dB HL at week 24 using the better treated ear.
results.quote: behavioural audiometry improving from greater than 96 ± 3 dB hearing level at baseline to 37 ± 5 dB hearing level at 2.5 years.

results.finding: In 12 children treated with DB-OTO, 67 adverse events occurred or worsened during or after treatment; none led to discontinued participation.
results.detail: The first-in-human study reports pediatric treatment and safety outcomes, but does not report completion of a 6-week dose-limiting toxicity assessment or the specified CTCAE toxicity thresholds.
results.quote: A total of 67 adverse events occurred or worsened during or after treatment, none of which led to discontinued participation in the study.

results.finding: In CHORD, 9 of 12 children (75%) achieved an average behavioral PTA threshold ≤70 dB HL at week 24 after DB-OTO.
results.quote: After a single infusion of DB-OTO, a PTA average threshold of 70 dB HL or less at week 24 (primary end point) and an auditory brain-stem response at or below 90 dB nHL (key secondary end point) were found in 9 of the 12 participants (75%;

results.finding: OTARMENI achieved average PTA ≤70 dB HL at week 24 in 16/20 children (80%); 24 children were treated.
results.detail: PTA averaged 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 kHz; bilateral recipients were evaluated using the better treated ear. One missing week-24 outcome was imputed as nonresponse.

results.finding: FDA granted OTARMENI accelerated approval in 2026, supported by a study of 24 treated children.
results.detail: The indication covers pediatric and adult patients with hearing loss >90 dB HL at any frequency, molecularly confirmed biallelic OTOF variants, preserved outer hair cell function and no prior cochlear implant in the same ear.
results.quote:
This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on the 
improvement of hearing sensitivity assessed by average pure tone audiometry 
(PTA) at Week 24.

results.finding: FDA licensed lunsotogene parvec-cwha (OTARMENI) on April 23, 2026, for OTOF-related hearing loss >90 dB HL; trial sample size is not reported.
results.detail: Accelerated approval covers pediatric and adult patients with molecularly confirmed biallelic OTOF variants, preserved outer hair cell function, and no prior cochlear implant in the same ear. The letter reports no week-24 hearing results; required confirmatory studies are future commitments.
results.quote:
Effective this date, we have approved your BLA for lunsotogene parvec-cwha (biologic) 
and the associated drug product Administration Kit (device), under accelerated approval

results.finding: OTOF gene transfer restored click ABR thresholds to 58.80 ± 1.07 dB SPL in treated Otof−/− mice (n=46).
results.detail: ABRs were measured four weeks after neonatal treatment using the mini-Myo15 promoter. Comparators included 8 untreated knockout and 13 wild-type mice. Thresholds required reproducible waveforms; auditory improvement persisted through 52 weeks, although wave I amplitudes remained below wild-type levels.
results.quote: the click ABR thresholds in the injected ear were restored to 58.80 ± 1.07 dB, which was about 20 dB higher the WT level

results.finding: OTOF gene transfer restored normal ABR thresholds in deaf Otof E1799del/E1799del mice, sustained for 3 months (treated groups: n=18 and n=4).
results.detail: Neonatal and adult treatment restored ABRs in a profoundly deaf mouse model with preserved outer hair cell function. ABR wave I amplitudes improved but remained below wild-type levels.
results.quote:
It is noteworthy that the restored hearing thresholds of treated
Otof
E1799del/E1799del
mice remained normal for at least 3 months post-injection, the last time point at which they were determined
